title: In-Context Impersonation Reveals Large Language Models’ Strengths and Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Prefixing prompts with gender personas (e.g., man, woman, agender, non-binary) to generate descriptions of objects, and measuring the resulting differences in downstream zero-shot visual classification accuracy across categories like birds, cars, aircraft, and flowers.

Prefixing prompts with racial identities (e.g., black, white, Asian, Indian, Hispanic) to generate object descriptions, and evaluating the downstream zero-shot visual classification performance to detect stereotypical associations (e.g., performance differences in describing cars vs. birds).

Prompting the LLM to impersonate people of different ages (e.g., 2, 4, 7, 13, and 20 years old) and evaluating the differences in vocabulary complexity, downstream visual classification accuracy, and simulated exploration/exploitation behaviors in a multi-armed bandit task.
